description: Add a one-shot startup reconciler that recovers system-update jobs left active (running/waiting-for-reconnect) by an interrupted prior server process: mark them failed and actually free the on-disk lock so a new update can start.

tasks.title: Add ReleaseStaleLockAsync to the system-update store
tasks.description: Add `ReleaseStaleLockAsync(string jobId, CancellationToken)` to `ISystemUpdateStore`. In `FileSystemSystemUpdateStore`, implement it by reusing the existing content-matched `ReleaseLockFile(jobId)` helper WITHOUT requiring the process-local `_lockOwnerJobId` to match (so it works in a freshly started process where `_lockOwnerJobId` is null). Mirror the same release semantics in the in-memory fake store used by specs. Cover with the existing temp-file lock-release pattern so a stale `.lock` file is deleted and a follow-up `TryAcquireLockAsync` on a fresh store instance succeeds. This is an additive capability; existing `ReleaseLockAsync` semantics stay untouched.
acceptanceCriteria: `FileSystemSystemUpdateStore.ReleaseStaleLockAsync` deletes the on-disk `.lock` file when its content matches `jobId`, independent of the in-memory `_lockOwnerJobId`, and is idempotent when the file is absent or held by a different owner.
The in-memory fake store mirrors the release behavior (releases when currently held by `jobId`, otherwise idempotent), preserving the `WaitForUnlockAsync` test signal.
Temp-file lock-release tests pass: a stale `.lock` file is removed and a subsequent `TryAcquireLockAsync` on a new store instance succeeds.
Existing `SourceAudit_ReleaseLockAsyncOnlyInSharedHelpersAndRunUpdateFinally` and other `FileSystemStore_*` / `SystemUpdateServiceSpecs` tests still pass (unchanged `ReleaseLockAsync` semantics).
tasks.output: Updated `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/SystemInfo/ISystemUpdateStore.cs` and `FileSystemSystemUpdateStore.cs`, mirrored fake store behavior, and new/updated lock-release tests.
tasks.notes: Design decision D2. Reuse the existing `ReleaseLockFile(jobId)` helper (:174-189) which already does the content match; only bypass the in-memory ownership gate. Do NOT loosen `ReleaseLockAsync` — that would risk the SourceAudit test and conflate in-process ownership release with post-restart cleanup.

tasks.title: Implement startup recovery for interrupted system-update jobs
tasks.description: Add `IProcessStartTimeProvider` (+ default `ProcessStartTimeProvider` that reads the actual process start time, the only place a real process-info read is allowed). Implement `SystemUpdateRecoveryService` as a direct `IHostedService` whose `StartAsync` runs once before the host serves requests: it reads the latest persisted job, and if `Status` is `running`/`waiting-for-reconnect` AND `UpdatedAt` strictly precedes the injected process start time, it builds the `failed` transition inline (reason = "interrupted by process restart", CompletedAt/UpdatedAt via `TimeProvider`), persists via `ISystemUpdateStore.SaveAsync`, and calls `ReleaseStaleLockAsync(jobId)`. Fresh active jobs and all terminal jobs are left untouched. Register `IProcessStartTimeProvider` (TryAddSingleton) and the reconciler (`AddHostedService`) in `MohistServiceRegistration.ConfigureMohistServices`. Add `Specs/SystemSpecs/SystemUpdateRecoverySpecs.cs` driving all spec scenarios with fake `TimeProvider` + injected process start time + the existing in-memory store fake.
acceptanceCriteria: `SystemUpdateRecoveryService` depends only on `ISystemUpdateStore`, `TimeProvider`, `IProcessStartTimeProvider`, and `ILogger`; it does NOT depend on `SystemUpdateService` and reads no wall clock / `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` / `Environment.TickCount` / process info directly.

A stale `running` job and a stale `waiting-for-reconnect` job (`UpdatedAt` strictly `<` process start time) are persisted as `failed` with `Reason` = "interrupted by process restart" and their lock is released via `ReleaseStaleLockAsync`.
When no job is persisted, the reconciler persists nothing and releases no lock (no-op).
A fresh active job (`UpdatedAt >=` process start time) is left in place and its lock is not released.
Any terminal job (`succeeded`/`failed`/`recovered`/`superseded`/`cancelled`) is never modified regardless of `UpdatedAt`.
After recovery, a fresh `SystemUpdateService.StartAsync` against the recovered store acquires the lock (`Started = true`) and does NOT return `update_in_progress`.

`MohistServiceRegistration.ConfigureMohistServices` registers `IProcessStartTimeProvider` with a default implementation (TryAddSingleton) and registers `SystemUpdateRecoveryService` via `AddHostedService`.
`Specs/SystemSpecs/SystemUpdateRecoverySpecs.cs` passes (Speed=Unit trait; fake time/store, no real fs/process/time); existing `SystemUpdateServiceSpecs` remain unchanged and passing.
tasks.output: New `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/SystemInfo/SystemUpdateRecoveryService.cs`, `IProcessStartTimeProvider.cs` + `ProcessStartTimeProvider.cs`, registration updates in `Infrastructure/Hosting/MohistServiceRegistration.cs`, and new `Specs/SystemSpecs/SystemUpdateRecoverySpecs.cs`.
tasks.notes: Design decisions D1, D3, D4, D5, D6, D7. Use a direct `IHostedService` (NOT BackgroundService) so the host awaits StartAsync before opening the HTTP listener — this closes the race where an early request still sees update_in_progress. The reconciler constructs the failed transition inline (D5); it must not call into SystemUpdateService. Reason text is the literal "interrupted by process restart" for stable assertions. Also covers requirements: #recovery-actually-frees-the-on-disk-lock-so-a-new-update-can-start, #fresh-active-jobs-and-terminal-jobs-are-never-modified, #the-process-start-time-is-sourced-through-an-injectable-abstraction.
